title: A Cellar for the Room
premise: Petra Eastwick, a forensic property surveyor, is sent to appraise Hollowmere House, a derelict estate whose cellar contains a bricked-up well and a nursery rhyme carved into the plaster. Her overnight audio monitoring rig records a second voice answering her spoken questions in her own cadence, and she learns the house was inherited by a family who hanged a servant girl, Maren, for theft she didn't commit — the song's verses recounting their crimes. Petra discovers she is Maren's collateral descendant and therefore the house's true heir; to end it, she must learn the song's suppressed final verse — the verse of forgiveness — and speak it into the well before dawn refills it with water and with Maren's rage. She does, at cost: the house releases its dead but claims her career, her skepticism, and her willingness to ever call any place empty again.
about_author: P. M. Underhill is the pen name of a former building inspector from the Yorkshire coast who spent eleven years surveying condemned properties before turning to fiction. Their stories are known for procedural precision applied to things that should not be procedure.

chapters.title: The Appraisal That Answers
chapters.summary: POV Petra. A skeptical surveyor arrives at Hollowmere House to value it for a bank, finding a sealed cellar well and a rhyme gouged into plaster. Doors she measures come out wrong by inches each time. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into the first crack in her certainty.

chapters.title: Overnight Recordings
chapters.summary: POV Petra. She leaves her audio rig running and plays back nine hours of silence except one segment: a second voice answering questions she doesn't remember asking, in her own voice. Emotional beat: cold dread; the rational mind constructing explanations that don't hold.

chapters.title: Maren of the Lower Floor
chapters.summary: POV alternating Petra and 1847 diary entries. Parish records reveal Maren Ash, a housemaid hanged for stealing silver later found sewn into the mistress's mattress. The song's early verses match the diary exactly. Emotional beat: horror becoming historical injustice; Petra begins caring.

chapters.title: Questions in the Dark
chapters.summary: POV Petra. She deliberately asks the recording questions; the voice answers, growing less like her and more desperate. It names the well, warns 'don't sing along,' and begs someone to finish the verse. Emotional beat: complicity — she realizes she's been chosen, not haunted.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: POV Petra with solicitor Halbrook. Deeds show every owner since 1847 died intestate or fled; a bloodline clause names 'the Eastwick issue' as true heirs. Petra's grandmother was an Eastwick of Hollowmere parish. Emotional beat: betrayal by genealogy; duty she never agreed to.

chapters.title: What the Well Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Petra. She unbricks the cellar and finds the well dry but warm, humming the tune. Touching the rim floods her with Maren's last night — the false accusation, the mistress's face. Emotional beat: grief and fury on behalf of a stranger who is not a stranger.

chapters.title: The Verse That Isn't Sung
chapters.summary: POV Halbrook. The solicitor, secretly a descendant of the accusing family, reveals the fourth verse was cut from every hymnal and ballad sheet: the verse where Maren forgives. His family has kept it unsung for six generations to keep the house cheap and quiet. Emotional beat: the banality of inherited guilt.

chapters.title: Refilling
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Water rises in the dry well overnight; recordings now sing all four known verses in chorus, faster each night. Halbrook tries to stop her, believing silence safer than mercy. Emotional beat: rising tempo, siege-like dread, resolve hardening into action.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: POV Petra. At the well's lip, water at her knees, she recites the forgiveness verse without singing it — speaking Maren's pardon as heir and judge both. The house convulses; the dead mistress surfaces in the water to be named and released too. Emotional beat: climax; justice outside law, delivered by choice rather than verdict.

chapters.title: A Cellar for the Room
chapters.summary: POV Petra, weeks later. The house appraises clean and ordinary; the well holds still, clear water. Petra files her report, keeps one recording, and takes a new job surveying places no one wants. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — belief arrived not as faith but as testimony.
